```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(appusageR)
data(appusage_demo)
```

This tutorial uses saved synthetic records, so diagnostics can be explored
without writing caches. Processing success, QC pass and grain eligibility answer
different questions.

## Keep the denominators visible

```{r qc}
quality <- lapply(names(appusage_demo$records), function(key) {
  record <- appusage_demo$records[[key]]
  id <- appusage_demo$sources$sequence_id[match(key, appusage_demo$sources$scenario)]
  assess_appusage_qc(record, metadata = record$metadata, participant_id = id)
})
qc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(quality, function(x) as.data.frame(x$qc)))
qc$participant_id <- appusage_demo$sources$sequence_id[
  match(names(appusage_demo$records), appusage_demo$sources$scenario)]
stopifnot(nrow(appusage_demo$sources) == 15L, length(quality) == 10L,
          sum(qc$pass_qc) == 5L, sum(!qc$pass_qc) == 5L)
qc[, c("participant_id", "pass_qc", "analysis_eligible_daily")]
```

Of 15 uploads, 10 reach research processing and QC. Five of those 10 pass QC;
the other five have deliberately short coverage. The five input failures are
not evaluated by QC. Read `analysis_eligible_event`, `analysis_eligible_episode`
and `analysis_eligible_daily` separately; an unavailable grain is not a failed
quality assessment of an observed grain. See `?assess_appusage_qc` for the fields.

## Recorded, explicit-empty and absent days

```{r days}
record <- appusage_demo$records$recorded_blank_absent_days
before <- record
observed <- audit_appusage_days(record, metadata = record$metadata)
zero <- audit_appusage_days(record, metadata = record$metadata, strategy = "zero_window")
observed$calendar
stopifnot(identical(observed$calendar$coverage,
                    c("recorded", "explicit_empty", "no_block", "recorded")),
          observed$denominator_days == 2L, observed$numerator_ms == 300000,
          observed$mean_ms == 150000, zero$denominator_days == 4L,
          zero$mean_ms == 75000, identical(record, before))
data.frame(strategy = c("observed_complete", "zero_window"),
           days = c(observed$denominator_days, zero$denominator_days),
           mean_minutes = c(observed$mean_ms, zero$mean_ms) / 60000)
```

The two recorded dates contain 2 and 3 minutes. Their mean is 2.5 minutes. The
explicit-empty date has a header but no records; the absent date has no block.
Treating both as zero is the explicit `zero_window` sensitivity assumption and
gives 1.25 minutes over four days. This view leaves saved durations and QC intact.

## Five kinds of interval overlap

```{r overlap, fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
record <- appusage_demo$records$overlapping_intervals
overlap <- audit_appusage_overlap(record, metadata = record$metadata)
overlap$pairs
stopifnot(identical(as.numeric(overlap$pairs$total), c(1, 2, 2, 2, 7)),
          overlap$totals[["stored_duration_sum"]] == 44000,
          overlap$totals[["endpoint_union"]] == 14000,
          overlap$totals[["multiplicity_excess"]] == 30000)
x <- record$data$episode
origin <- min(x$start_ts_ms)
plot(c(0, 14), c(1, nrow(x)), type = "n", ylab = "Synthetic interval",
     xlab = "Seconds from first start")
segments((x$start_ts_ms-origin)/1000, seq_len(nrow(x)),
         (x$end_ts_ms-origin)/1000, seq_len(nrow(x)), lwd = 3)
```

The six intervals are `(0,10)`, `(0,10)`, `(0,6)`, `(4,10)`, `(3,7)` and `(6,14)`.
Their durations sum to 44 seconds, while the union spans 14 seconds. The extra
30 seconds express multiplicity. Pair counts classify identical endpoints,
same start, same end, strict containment and partial crossing. Optional
`strategy = "equal_share"` or `"priority"` returns an allocation view under the
specified assumption; neither changes the stored scientific tables.

## Midnight splitting

```{r midnight}
midnight <- appusage_demo$records$cross_midnight$data
midnight$daily[, c("date", "duration_ms")]
stopifnot(identical(as.numeric(midnight$daily$duration_ms), c(300000, 420000)),
          sum(midnight$daily$duration_ms) == sum(midnight$episode$duration_ms))
```

The ten-minute interval at 23:55 contributes five minutes to each date; a separate
two-minute interval adds to the second day. Native-block day auditing describes
the source table's date; standardized daily aggregation splits intervals at
local midnight. These are distinct, named views.
